brief: TS Lombard's Steven Blitz argues the 10Y yield, which hit 5.30% Wednesday (highest since 2002), goes past the 6% many now expect: 5.75% is the next plateau, 8% the long-run target over a few years. His chain starts with the Fed's "original sin," easing before a downturn fully kills inflation. Powell eased late last year under political pressure despite rising profits, so the 2025 recession never arrived: fiscal expansion and tariffs offset a 22-month inverted curve and declining private payrolls ex-hospitals. Per Blitz's adages, profits lead employment, employment leads inflation, and 2026 was the recovery's good year. From here, rising profits imply faster hiring and higher base inflation in 2027. Behind the yield rise is too much DM sovereign debt supply against deficits outrunning GDP, with no central bank absorbing the excess. Swap spreads show investors increasingly prefer floating SOFR to fixed USTs, a fiscal-risk preference, not a curve issue. Easy money plus bigger deficits means higher inflation and yields each cycle until there is political will to accept a growth hit, not expected before 2029. What breaks is the market's confidence that inflation returns to 2% and that stocks and bonds always reward the long side, not a specific asset.
